generatedProse.concept-context: In any subject where a module covers a wide spread of material, having no revision plan is a fast route to anxiety. The content feels endless, and last-minute reading rarely sticks. A simple strategy, sharing your time across topics and finding where your understanding is thin, replaces that dread with manageable steps.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two students who have the same exam in two weeks.

Student A has no plan. They tell themselves the deadline is far off, then realise late how much there is to cover. The last few days become a rush of rereading, long into the night. They arrive exhausted and anxious, unsure what has gone in.

Student B makes a simple plan. They list the topics, check which ideas they cannot yet explain, and spread their time across the two weeks, giving the weak spots more attention. They still feel nervous, but the nerves are manageable, because they know they have covered the ground.

Both wanted to do well. Only Student B had a strategy, and it was the strategy that kept the anxiety in check.
generatedProse.summary: Much exam anxiety grows from having no revision strategy, and a strategy is simply a plan for how you prepare. An effective plan rests on using your time well and finding the gaps in your understanding. You can now explain why a strategy matters, recognise how it eases anxiety, and name an early step towards one. That is the foundation later courses build on.

check.body: In the worked example, what helped Student B feel calmer going into the exam?

items.text: They had a plan that used their time and targeted the ideas they could not yet explain.
They simply worried less and hoped for the best.
They left all their revision until the night before.
They decided the exam did not matter to them.

feedback.correct: That's right. A plan that used their time and targeted their gaps left Student B feeling prepared.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Student B did that Student A did not.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Student B felt calmer because they had a strategy: it used their time and found their gaps. Hoping, cramming or not caring are not what helped.
